newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan expects to export sugar in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan expects to export sugar in 1997/98.

text.p: The Pakistan Sugar Mills Association (PSMA) said on Monday that the 1997/98 (July-June) crop was likely to yield three million tonnes of sugar, of which 300,000 tonnes could be exported.
"Sugar mills will produce three million tonnes this year mainly because more sugarcane is available after monsoon rains," PSMA secretary general Khadim Ali Qazilbash told Reuters.
He said the rains augured well for a bumper crop in water-short Sindh, Punjab and North West Frontier provinces.
"We have happily informed the government today the country will harvest a very good sugarcane crop this year. We will easily achieve a production target of three million tonnes."
Out of Pakistan's 75 mills, 68 would start sugarcane crushing from November, he said.
He forecast domestic consumption at 2.7 million tonnes in 1997/98, leaving 300,000 as an exportable surplus.
Qazilbash said some 700,000 tonnes of 1996/97 sugar was still in the mills, enough to meet demand till November.
Dealers were lifting 60,000 to 70,000 tonnes of sugar a month from mills, much less than the normal average of 140,000, with the balance drawn from imported sugar, he said.

Importers had opened letters of credit to import another 170,000 tonnes, but it was not clear if all this would be imported. "If the locally produced and imported sugar reaches Pakistan, we will have a sugar glut," Qazilbash said.
At least three ships with 39,155 tonnes of sugar reached Karachi port last week, a port official said.
Pakistan imported 596,467 tonnes of sugar worth $227 million in 1996/97. Hardly any was imported the previous year.
The PSMA said production had reached 2.393 million tonnes by June 30 compared to 2.47 million at the same time a year ago and 3.0 million in 1994/95.
